claims.title: Zero-error encoder and confusion-graph coloring equivalence
claims.scope: one finite source-state set, one common deterministic one-shot message, finitely many sinks, exact finite target functions, and exact local side-information functions
assumptions: the encoder message is fixed before each sink decodes
sink t decodes only from the common message and its declared side-information value
every demanded target must be recovered with zero error for every source state
nonclaims: the theorem does not cover interaction, allowed error, quantum messages, or asymptotic block coding
graph colors are message labels rather than physical states of an unknown parent substrate

claims.title: Exact one-shot message alphabet equals chromatic number
claims.scope: the finite deterministic zero-error common-message function problem represented by its confusion graph G
assumptions: one message value is used per source state in one execution
fixed-length bits use an injective binary representation of the message alphabet
nonclaims: chromatic number is not asserted to equal an expected variable-length rate under a source prior
one-shot fixed-length cost is not an asymptotic graph-entropy theorem

claims.title: Clique and independence lower bounds for predictive messages
claims.scope: one finite confusion graph with maximum clique size omega and maximum independent-set size alpha
assumptions: each message class is an independent vertex set
the source-state set is finite and nonempty
nonclaims: either lower bound can be loose for a selected graph
the bounded exact clique and independent-set algorithms are not claimed efficient on arbitrary large graphs

claims.title: Universal finite graph realization by side-information demands
claims.scope: every finite simple graph, realized as a finite zero-error common-message function problem with one constructed sink per graph edge
assumptions: constructed side-information values may be arbitrary finite hashable labels
every non-endpoint vertex receives a unique side-information value at the edge sink
nonclaims: the construction is not asserted to be a natural physical realization of every graph
the theorem does not imply every structured physical query family has arbitrary graph complexity

claims.title: Zero-error private randomization does not reduce one-shot message alphabet
claims.scope: one finite confusion graph with a private randomized encoder represented by a nonempty support of messages for every source state
assumptions: adjacent source states must have disjoint message supports for zero error
the decoder does not receive an additional source-dependent variable beyond the sampled message and declared side information
nonclaims: the theorem does not cover allowed error, shared source-dependent randomness, variable expected length, or quantum encodings
selecting one support element proves an alphabet lower bound rather than an equality of all randomized performance criteria

claims.title: Side-information refinement contracts confusion
claims.scope: two finite function problems with identical states, sinks, and targets, where equality of refined side values implies equality of coarse side values
assumptions: side-information refinement is checked for every sink and source-state pair
both problems use the same one-shot deterministic zero-error interface
nonclaims: more informative side information is an explicit resource and is not declared free
edge deletion can leave chromatic number unchanged even when some ambiguity is removed

claims.title: Target coarsening contracts confusion
claims.scope: two finite function problems with identical states, sinks, and side information, where each new target is a function of the corresponding original target
assumptions: target coarsening is checked on every finite source-state pair
the decoder is only required to recover the coarsened target in the transformed problem
nonclaims: a cheaper coarsened target does not establish the same cost for the original detailed target
the theorem does not compare unrelated target recodings that fail the finite functional-coarsening condition

claims.title: Confusion-color multicast bridge
claims.scope: one finite confusion-graph function problem with chi colors and one already certified exact h-symbol common-demand multicast code over F_p satisfying chi at most p^h
assumptions: every function sink recovers the complete finite-field source vector
color labels are injected into distinct field vectors
each sink retains its declared exact local side information
nonclaims: multicasting the full color is not claimed optimal among all sink-specific network function codes
the field embedding is a coding convention rather than physical ontology

claims.title: Two-bit side-information chromatic phase change
claims.scope: two binary source coordinates with t1 demanding x1 and t2 demanding x2, first with no side information and then with each sink knowing the other coordinate
assumptions: the common encoder is one-shot, deterministic, and zero error
complementary side information is exact and causally available at decoding time
nonclaims: the one-bit parity gain is conditional on complementary side information
the example is not a general nonlinear index-coding capacity theorem

claims.title: Bounded exact confusion-graph algorithm certificate
claims.scope: bounded finite graphs below the declared vertex cap, including exhaustive comparison on every labeled four-vertex simple graph
assumptions: exact k-colorability search exhausts every smaller color limit before returning the optimum
maximum clique and independent-set searches remain within the configured finite cap
direct brute-force tests enumerate all 64 labeled four-vertex graphs
nonclaims: bounded exhaustive agreement is not a scalability claim for large graphs
a configured vertex-cap rejection is not an impossibility or optimum result
